title: Three-Way Valve

introduction.definition: A three-way valve has three ports. Used as a diverting valve it sends one inlet to either of two outlets; used as a mixing valve it combines two inlets into one outlet. The L-port ball valve modelled connects the bottom inlet to outlet A or outlet B as the ball is rotated.
applications: Diverting flow between two units (duty/standby filters, heat-exchanger bypass)
Temperature control by mixing hot and cold streams
key_points: L-port: one path at a time; T-port: can connect all three
Port/flow pattern must be checked on the chart
Lever pointer shows the flow path

foundation: Support the valve and adjoining pipe so the body does not carry pipe weight or thermal loads; heavy valves need their own supports.
alignment: Align flanges face-to-face and bore-to-bore before bolting; never pull pipes into place with the bolts.
Respect the flow-direction arrow on the body.
piping: Flush the line before installing the valve so welding debris cannot damage seats.
Provide isolation and drain/vent points for maintenance.
Allow access for the handwheel/actuator and for removal of internals.
commissioning: Check the valve strokes fully and smoothly.
Pressure-test the line (shell test) with the valve partly open; do not use the valve to blind a test above its seat rating.
Record the as-installed position and set points.

routine.task: Check lever position matches the required path.

periodic.task: Operate through full travel to prevent sticking.

lubrication: Lubricate stem threads and operator gearing per the manufacturer; most wetted internals need no lubrication.

video_tutorials.title: Three-Way Valve — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Three-Way Valve.
A three-way valve has three ports.
Used as a diverting valve it sends one inlet to either of two outlets; used as a mixing valve it combines two inlets into one outlet.
The L-port ball valve modelled connects the bottom inlet to outlet A or outlet B as the ball is rotated.

Typical applications include diverting flow between two units (duty/standby filters, heat-exchanger bypass); temperature control by mixing hot and cold streams; sampling and tank selection; hydraulic and pneumatic switching.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Valve Body (Three Ports) with Flanges.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Three-Way Valve — Operation

script.narration: How the Three-Way Valve works.
Flow enters the bottom port.
The L-shaped bore in the ball connects the inlet to outlet A.
Rotating the lever turns the ball inside its seats.
Now the bore connects the inlet to outlet B; outlet A is shut.
PTFE seats seal against the ball.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Three-Way Valve — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Three-Way Valve.
Check lever position matches the required path.
Operate through full travel to prevent sticking.
Replace seats and stem seals.
Watch for cross-port leakage: flow to the wrong outlet. Common cause: worn seats.
Watch for wrong flow path: process upset. Common cause: wrong port pattern or orientation.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
